PullRequest.Title: Use distinct AppUserModelID in portable mode on Windows
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #337679

In portable mode on Windows, use `${win32AppUserModelId}.Portable` as the AppUserModelID instead of the same id as the installed product.

Windows groups, pins and builds jump lists by AppUserModelID, not by executable path. Because a portable copy shared the id with an installed copy (which is also stamped on installer-created shortcuts and file association ProgIDs):

- Pinning a running portable window pinned the installed copy's Start menu shortcut.
- The taskbar jump list ("New Window", "Agents Window", recent folders/files) was the one written by the installed copy, launching the installed exe. Portable mode intentionally skips `setJumpList` / `addRecentDocument`, so it never replaced it.
- Portable and installed windows were grouped together on the taskbar.

With a distinct id, portable VS Code is treated as a separate app: pins point to the portable exe and it no longer inherits the installed copy's jump list.

Notes:
- Portable mode still does not register a jump list or recent documents (unchanged, to avoid leaving traces).
- Native toast notifications from a portable instance can no longer piggy-back on the installed Start menu shortcut's AUMID registration; this matches the behavior of a portable copy on a machine without VS Code installed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Windows primary-process startup in portable and installed modes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the process claims the single-instance IPC server, CodeApplication.startup synchronously selects the AUMID and calls Electron's app.setAppUserModelId before continuing startup. The diff adds only a memoized environment lookup and, in portable mode, one short string construction; both are on the startup critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronous Electron native call app.setAppUserModelId to set the Windows process AUMID.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one call per primary-process startup on Windows when win32AppUserModelId is configured, independent of window, workspace, or history size.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same native API was called once at the same point with win32AppUserModelId. Portable startup now passes a suffixed ID; installed startup passes the identical prior value.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The native call must finish before startup proceeds, but the diff does not add a call or move it; it only changes the portable-mode argument.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work per primary-process startup. The only new allocation is `${win32AppUserModelId}.Portable` for portable mode, whose size scales only with the small product identifier and is created once.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One CodeApplication startup and one setAppUserModelId call per successfully claimed primary process. Secondary launches that fail the instance claim do not reach this code; there is no loop, queue, or parallel fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: EnvironmentMainService.isPortable is memoized. Its cold access reads VSCODE_PORTABLE once; later accesses use the memoized boolean. There is no cache key, miss retry, negative-cache, or coalescing behavior affected by the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed hunk, the memoized isPortable getter, and the single CodeApplication construction after claimInstance.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact native-call duration is not measured, but call count and placement are unchanged; the added lookup and bounded string allocation are negligible and non-scaling.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: portable startup retains the existing one-call native boundary and adds only constant, bounded argument selection; installed startup behavior and cost are effectively unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full one-file, one-hunk diff. Traced startup ownership, accessor cost, native boundary cardinality, cache behavior, and concurrency; no actionable diff-introduced performance issue or shipped performance-regression fix was found.
